Hi Elena — thanks for the clear options. A couple of procurement notes and the path we recommend to reduce hold time: 

1) Conditional PO: We can issue a conditional PO for a limited pilot amount (USD 25,000) on receipt of either a notarized W-8BEN-E scan OR a DocuSign envelope that includes e-notarization. The PO will be marked "Pending Tax Validation" and will convert to a firm PO once our tax team confirms the FTIN matches the W-8 details.

2) Bank letter: please include the bank letter on bank letterhead with account number masked to last 4 digits, and an issuance date within the last 90 days. That will allow payments team to provision ACH/FP/virtual card options.

3) FTIN format: numeric-only is preferred for our verification system — please send the RUT without punctuation as a separate line (e.g., 123456789). If your tax counsel can confirm the FTIN maps to the W-8 legal name that speeds the check.

4) DocuSign: We can send our standard DocuSign envelope that includes e-notary. It’s usually the fastest for international entities who use electronic notarization. If you prefer the wet-notary scan, please send as soon as available.

Estimated timeline if you send the DocuSign e-notary link today: PO conditional issuance within 24 hours, final PO within 48–72 hours after tax verification. If you send a wet-signed notarized PDF today, timeline is similar once we receive the scan.

Priyom (tax) — can you confirm the automated FTIN check tolerance for Chilean RUT? If manual review needed, flag SLA to 72 hours.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
